To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people are willing to pay for water quality improvements in rivers, that the distance decay effect is relevant and that the state of residency matters.

(1) people would significantly benefit if the water quality in the region is improved, (2) accounting for the spatial context is crucial to derive welfare measures and (3) the extent of the markets varies with respect to river stretches and water quality levels.
the CV measures for the three rivers differ substantially, the extent of the markets varies, and the welfare measures are affected by the spatial context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial context and how it affects the valuation of environmental improvements.
the spatial context of water quality improvement projects and the resulting welfare implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water quality improvements are beneficial for the population of Berlin–Brandenburg.
the welfare measures are sensitive to the spatial context and to the choice of model specification.
the welfare gains of improved water quality would be higher if the state of Brandenburg would improve its river sections more than the state of Berlin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial context should not be ignored and that the distance to the river and the state of residency should be included in the analysis.
the distance to the river stretch and the residency of the respondent have to be taken into account to obtain valid welfare measures.
water quality improvements are valued differently depending on the spatial context, and, therefore, the spatial context should be considered when estimating willingness to pay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial context matters and needs to be considered when estimating willingness to pay for water quality improvements in regions that are common to several Lander.
spatial effects should be accounted for in the context of water quality valuation.
it is important to consider the spatial context when estimating welfare effects in the context of water quality.
